title: PFT: Phonon Fine-tuning for Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials
claim: Force constants can come from supercell finite differences, or from model Hessians; we supervise sampled Hessian columns efficiently via hessian-vector products.
layout: 3 panels; panel c has four parallel columns feeding a bottom loss equation
description: Panel a shows a small blue atomic unitcell with a down arrow to a much larger supercell lattice. Panel b shows pretraining on a unitcell: a DFT box branching into energy E, forces F and stress sigma. Panel c is the main part. Four parallel columns (i–iv) each start from a pink Supercell box. i uses DFT on finite displacements to give a force-constant heatmap. ii uses an MLIP with negative energy gradients to give predicted force constants. iii uses an MLIP with the analytical Hessian to give a full Hessian heatmap. iv uses an MLIP with a hessian-vector product to give a single Hessian column. A bottom panel samples a column from the DFT matrix and compares it with the MLIP column in the L_PFT equation, which adds energy, force and stress terms. Purple marks DFT and orange marks MLIP. The magma-colored heatmaps draw the eye first.
caption: Overview of PFT framework. a Finite-difference calculations rely on the construction of a supercell to obtain force constants from interactions beyond the unitcell. b MLIPs are pre-trained on standard unitcell DFT calculations. c-i Up to $O(3N)$ atomic displacements are applied to the supercell, with the number reduced by crystal symmetries; forces are computed with DFT, and numerical derivatives yield the force-constant matrix. c-ii The same workflow can be used for MLIPs, replacing DFT force calculations with force predictions from the model. c-iii Alternatively, the force constants can also be computed as the analytical Hessian of the predicted energy directly. c-iv In this work, we use the Hessian-vector product to efficiently compute columns of the Hessian, and align with sampled DFT force constant columns during training. Note the shown force constants are downsampled for clarity.
abstract: Many materials properties depend on higher-order derivatives of the potential energy surface, yet machine learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) trained with a standard loss on energy, force, and stress errors can exhibit error in curvature, degrading the prediction of vibrational properties. We introduce phonon fine-tuning (PFT), which directly supervises second-order force constants of materials by matching MLIP energy Hessians to DFT-computed force constants from finite displacement phonon calculations. To scale to large supercells, PFT stochastically samples Hessian columns and computes the loss with a single Hessian-vector product. We also use a simple co-training scheme to incorporate upstream data to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. On the MDR Phonon benchmark, PFT improves Nequix MP by 55% on average across phonon thermodynamic properties and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy among models trained on Materials Project trajectories. PFT also generalizes to improve properties beyond second-derivatives, improving thermal conductivity predictions that rely on third-order derivatives of the potential energy.
